what: MetLife is one of the largest life insurers in the world. Its biggest business is group benefits: the life, dental, disability and accident insurance that American employers provide to staff. It also sells retirement products and insurance across Asia and Latin America.
customers: Employers buying group benefits for staff, individuals buying insurance and annuities, and institutional clients.
money: workplace life, dental, disability and accident insurance in the US
pension risk transfer, annuities and stable value products
insurance in Japan, Korea and other Asian markets
moat: Employer relationships that renew year after year, and an investment portfolio large enough to earn spreads that smaller insurers cannot.
risks: Insurance earnings depend on claims experience, which can turn sharply
Falling interest rates reduce the income earned on invested premiums
Its investment portfolio includes commercial property loans
Currency moves in Japan and Latin America affect results
opportunities: Group benefits is steady and grows with employment and wages
Pension risk transfer demand rises as companies offload pension obligations
Return on invested capital near 10% with large ongoing buybacks
watch: Group benefits claims ratio and net investment income.
